# `Q-26-1` — Lua syntax error in an lmd cell

> The Lua in an lmd cell does not parse, so the cell cannot be desugared. The cell is left as written and does not run.

## What this means

Before an lmd cell runs, Quarto *desugars* it: it parses the cell as Lua,
finds every markdown fragment (`{=: … :=}`, `{=[ … ]=}`, `{= … =}`) and
rewrites each one into `pandoc.*` constructor calls. That parse found a
Lua syntax error, so nothing in the cell could be rewritten and the cell
was not run. It stays in the rendered document as a plain code block, so
you can see what was written.

The warning points at the line and column of the error, counted inside
the cell.

## Why this happens

- An ordinary Lua typo: a missing `end`, an unbalanced parenthesis, a
  stray operator at the end of a line.
- A fragment that was never closed. `{=:` must end with `:=}`, `{=[` with
  `]=}`, and `{=` with `=}`; a fragment closed with the wrong delimiter
  swallows the rest of the cell and the Lua after it no longer parses.
- A fragment written where Lua does not allow an expression, for
  example as a statement on its own line. A fragment is a value; assign
  it, return it, or pass it to a function.

## How to fix

Read the position in the warning, correct the Lua, and render again. If
the position is right after a fragment, check the fragment's closing
delimiter first.

````markdown
```{lmd}
local x = 1
return {= a =} +
```
````

The trailing `+` has no right operand. Delete it, or finish the
expression.

- [`Q-26-2`](Q-26-2.qmd): the Lua parsed, but a fragment contains
  markdown the cell cannot build.
